event_note: Infosys press release of 2026-10-19 (https://www.infosys.com/newsroom/press-releases/documents/2026/q2-oct23-2026.pdf; restated by BusinessToday 2026-10-22): Q2 FY27 results at about 15:45 IST on Fri 2026-10-23, which is about 06:15 ET, before the US open and after the 15:30 IST NSE close. The ADR is the first venue to trade the release, inside the window from the 10-22 close to the 10-23 close. NSE shares react on Monday 10-26, after the window.
conviction_note: The FY27 guide decides this print. The street is split between a trim to 1.5-2.5% (Emkay) and a narrowing to 2-3% (HDFC), and the ADR has fallen on 3 of the last 4 guidance updates that were not outright raises. Against that, the ADR is up 24% in 20 days on a sector-wide rally after Accenture, short interest is 109M ADRs (7.4 days to cover), and every peer print this month except Wipro's was bought. The findings net to 0.0. The scaled number (-0.42) leans slightly down because the guide trim is the modal outcome, but the bar is disputed and a crowded short sits against a negative, so p_up is 47 and not lower.
bar: Q2 FY27 revenue Rs 49,108 cr, PAT Rs 7,904 cr and operating margin 21.2% (Bloomberg consensus, BusinessToday 2026-10-22, https://www.businesstoday.in/markets/stocks/story/infosys-q2-results-dividend-earnings-expectations-timing-fy27-guidance-targets-563068-2026-10-22). Constant-currency QoQ estimates run 1.1-1.7%, including about 50bp from Optimum (TradingView/businessline poll, https://www.tradingview.com/news/moodys:5f90fa053e78c:0-infosys-q2-revenue-growth-likely-to-remain-modest-analysts-see-guidance-cut/); Kotak puts organic at 1.1%. The two revenue sources agree. The GUIDANCE bar is disputed: the current guide is 1.5-3.0% cc with a 20-22% margin; Emkay expects 1.5-2.5% and HDFC expects 2-3% (the article calls this 'lowered by 50bp', which its own numbers contradict). Guidance-line findings are therefore capped small. Large-deal TCV is expected at $2-3bn (HDFC), against $3.6bn in Q1.
positioning_check: Short interest on the INFY ADR was 108,980,731 shares at the 2026-09-30 settlement, 7.39 days to cover, down from 125.1M (9/15) and 129.8M (8/31) (https://equibles.com/stocks/infy/shortinterest, read 2026-10-22; FINRA publishes 10/15 on 10/26). Against the baseline's 20.9M 20-day average volume that is about 5.2 days. ADR shorts partly hedge arbitrage against the NSE line, so the share that is directional is unknown. Precedent: on 2025-12-19 a recall-driven squeeze took the ADR up about 40% intraday (https://letsdatascience.com/news/infosys-adrs-surge-following-accenture-revenue-beat-bc5dd881). Options: 25-delta skew +5.08 vol points (downside paid), put/call OI 1.21, event-implied move 7.22% (baseline). The skew and a negative guidance read point the same way, so the downside is partly priced; the large, still-covering short is the offsetting mechanism.

findings.finding: The FY27 guide is expected to be cut or narrowed from 1.5-3.0% cc: Emkay says 1.5-2.5% (midpoint down 25bp to 2%, excluding Versent), HDFC says 2-3%. The INFY ADR fell after 3 of the last 4 guidance updates that were not outright raises: Oct-2025 narrowing to 2-3% about -2.25%, Apr-2026 first FY27 guide of 1.5-3.5% about -4%, Jul-2026 top-end trim to 1.5-3% -2.0% close ($10.71). The one gain was Jan-2026, when FY26 guidance was raised to 3-3.5% (ADR -2%, then +10.4% the next session).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Rebuilt from confirmed releases, not the baseline's 6-K matches. Oct-2025 guide narrowed up, ADR -2.25% (https://www.samco.in/knowledge-center/articles/infosys-share-price-dips-after-q2-results-revenue-and-profit-rise-despite-market-reaction/). Jan-2026 guide raised, ADR +10.4% (https://www.businesstoday.in/amp/markets/stocks/story/infosys-q3-results-adrs-up-10-share-price-targets-post-fy26-guidance-revision-510980-2026-01-15). Apr-2026 guide 1.5-3.5%, ADR -4% (https://www.businesstoday.in/amp/markets/stocks/story/infosys-shares-in-focus-as-adrs-fall-4-overnight-heres-why-fresh-target-prices-527214-2026-04-24). Jul-2026 top end trimmed, ADR -2.0% close, -5.8% intraday (https://www.venturasecurities.com/news/stocks/infosys-share-price-falls-2-5-after-q1-fy27-results-guidance-cut-and-ceo-transition-announcement/).
findings.why_not_priced: A trim is the published base case, so part of it is priced: the skew is +5 vol points and P/C OI is 1.21. But the stock has risen about 12% on NSE since 10-5 (Rs 1,033.75 to Rs 1,156) and the ADR 24% in 20 days, on sector momentum rather than on any Infosys-specific upgrade. A price that already held a trim would not have rallied into it. The two brokers' expected ranges (1.5-2.5% against 2-3%) differ by the width of a typical reaction, so the outcome is not settled.
findings.independence: Outlook Business 2026-07-24 says the July cut was 'sharper than analysts expected' and brokers said execution must improve to meet even the revised band (https://www.outlookbusiness.com/markets/infosys-slides-2-as-q1-miss-guidance-cut-weigh-on-sentiment). The same reaction-history sources as above. HDFC's 2-3% expectation points the other way.

findings.finding: The run-up is a sector rally, not an Infosys re-rating. Accenture's FY26 Q4 beat on 2026-10-01 (revenue $18.68bn against $18.03bn expected, FY27 guide 3-6% local currency) lifted INFY ADRs about 8% in a week. TCS, Infosys, HCLTech and Wipro then rose 12-13% in the week of 10-13 to 10-16, and Infosys gave back about 2.5% on 10-19. Commentators (Religare, Master Capital) called it a tactical rally from a sector that was down about 25% year to date.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: In Jul-2026 the stock had also risen into the print (Jefferies sector upgrade, Infosys up 3.8% on 07-27 per BusinessToday) and fell 2% on the guide. No clean history of a 20%+ run-up into an Infosys print.
findings.why_not_priced: The run-up itself is in the baseline. The finding is that the run-up rests on a peer's demand signal and not on Infosys's own numbers, and Kotak's piece still forecasts large-cap organic growth of about 0.5% and AI-led net deflation of about 3.5%. If the market had priced Infosys's own guide risk, the stock would not have outrun the sector into the print.
findings.independence: TradingView/Mint round-up of the October IT rally and analysts' 'tactical' label (https://www.tradingview.com/news/moodys:97c2d2f27100d:0-tcs-infosys-wipro-shares-ahead-of-q2-results-explained-what-accenture-s-strong-earnings-mean-for-indian-it-stocks/). This shares the baseline's run-up number, so it is sized small.

findings.finding: The short is still crowded and was covering into the print: ADR short interest of 108.98M at 2026-09-30 (7.39 days to cover), down from 129.8M at 08-31, before most of the October rally. The ADR has squeezed violently before (2025-12-19, about 40% intraday on a recall, two LULD halts).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: 2025-12-19: the ADR spiked about 40% intraday and closed +5.4% at $20.22 on a short squeeze tied to a recall (https://letsdatascience.com/news/infosys-adrs-surge-following-accenture-revenue-beat-bc5dd881). There is no earnings-day squeeze on record.
findings.why_not_priced: The baseline carries no short interest, and a +5 vol-point put skew prices the downside path without pricing a squeeze on a 'less bad' guide. If the squeeze were priced, call skew would be bid and the skew would be flat or negative.
findings.independence: None from a different source. Part of the ADR short hedges the NSE line in arbitrage, which dilutes the squeeze mechanism.

findings.finding: Q2 headline revenue gets mechanical help that the organic number does not show: about 50bp from a full quarter of Optimum Healthcare IT (closed 2026-05-05, up to $465m consideration) plus about 50bp from the absence of Q1's one-off EURS program-termination revenue reversal. Kotak expects a 50bp swing in post-sales support provisions to offset part of this. The headline can therefore print at the top of the 1.1-1.7% cc QoQ range while organic stays about 1%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Jan-2026: a profit miss on a one-off was looked through for the guide (ADR +10%). Jul-2026: a revenue miss with a cited 50bp one-off was sold (-2%). Quarter-line surprises have mattered less than the guide.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: Emkay and Kotak both model it. Filed small because the headline-versus-organic gap is the kind of thing that moves the first minutes of the ADR before the call clarifies it. The Q1 one-off is documented in the Q1 call coverage (https://upstox.com/news/market-news/earnings/infosys-q1-results-fy-27-revenue-growth-guidance-narrowed-to-1-5-3-0-in-constant-currency/article-197461/).
findings.independence: Infosys's own release for Optimum (https://www.infosys.com/newsroom/press-releases/2026/completes-acquisition-optimum-healthcare-it.html) and the Q1 FY27 6-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001067491/000106749126000038/exv99w01.htm). Shares the BusinessToday document with finding 1.

findings.finding: Peers that reported after Infosys last spoke mostly printed 'less bad' and were bought. HCLTech raised the bottom of its FY27 cc guide to 2.5-4% (from 1-4%) with bookings of $3.26bn, +27% YoY, and rallied. TCS printed only +0.5% cc QoQ but TCV of $9.6bn and rose 5.5%. Tech Mahindra beat with $1.02bn of deals and rose about 7.5%. The exception was Wipro: it guided Q3 to -1.5% to +0.5% cc with large-deal bookings down 58.6% QoQ, and the ADR fell about 1-3%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: October 2026 peer reactions: TCS +5.5% (https://www.indiainfoline.com/news/companies/tcs-share-price-jumps-5-46-after-q2-fy27-results-net-profit-rises-4-qoq-to-13884-crore), HCLTech rallied on 10-13 (https://www.equentis.com/blog/?p=71068), TechM +7.5% (https://hdfcsky.com/news/tech-mahindra-q2-results-shares-rise-7-46-percent-as-profit-jumps-32-7-percent), Wipro ADR down on its Q3 guide (https://www.goodreturns.in/news/wipro-q2-results-pat-drops-4-5-qoq-revenue-up-9-yoy-wipro-adr-crashes-3-on-q3-guidance-1541797.html).
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced through the sector rally. What is not settled is the reaction function: this month the market rewarded HCLTech's raised floor and punished Wipro's soft guide. That makes the guide the switch for Infosys, consistent with finding 1. Filed small and positive because 3 of 4 peers were bought on modest numbers.
findings.independence: Each peer is a separate primary print. This bears on the same guidance switch as finding 1 from the opposite side; they do not contradict each other, because finding 1 is the guide outcome and this is the market's current tolerance.

findings.finding: Wage hikes start in Q3: most employees get raises in October and senior staff in January, in phases, per the Q1 FY27 press conference. The 20-22% margin guide is expected to be held (Emkay, HDFC), but the commentary on the Q3 margin path will carry the hike plus furloughs, which Wipro's Q3 guide also cited.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Margins have been 'resilient' and the margin guide unchanged for four quarters. Margin commentary has not been the line that moved the ADR.
findings.why_not_priced: It is known and modelled. HDFC expects rupee depreciation and the staggered hikes to keep the margin guide stable. Filed small because a Q3 margin step-down in the call could cap any guidance relief.
findings.independence: Wipro's Q3 guide cites seasonal furloughs (https://www.goodreturns.in/news/wipro-q2-results-pat-drops-4-5-qoq-revenue-up-9-yoy-wipro-adr-crashes-3-on-q3-guidance-1541797.html).

outside_window.finding: NSE-listed Infosys shares react on Monday 2026-10-26 because the release lands after the 15:30 IST close. Any ADR-to-NSE premium or discount resolves after this window. FINRA's 10/15 short-interest print is published 10/26.

searched_and_found_nothing: Infosys-specific large-deal announcements in Aug-Oct 2026: none found beyond the Q1 disclosures and the January NHS deal
Versent (75% of Telstra's unit) closing status: no completion announcement found; Emkay excludes it from the guide
Buyback expectations: none mentioned in any preview; the board considers only an interim dividend 'if any'
LTIMindtree Q2 FY27 numbers: not surfaced
Hiring and job signals: only the 20,000-fresher plan and a 6k FDE hiring headline (Deccan Herald), no new change
Cognizant, Capgemini and EPAM Q3 prints: not yet out, all fall after the window

rejected_candidates.detail: The sweep flags baseline_history_trustworthy=false (6-K matches at a 15-day cadence). The actual release dates (2025-10-16, 2026-01-14, 2026-04-23, 2026-07-23) do not match the baseline's dates. It was replaced by the rebuilt history in finding 1.

rejected_candidates.candidate: HDFC's guide expectation described as 'lowered by 50bp to 2-3% from 1.5-3%'
rejected_candidates.detail: Internally inconsistent: 2-3% raises the floor and does not cut. It is folded into finding 1 as evidence that the guide bar is disputed, not filed as a separate negative.

rejected_candidates.candidate: CEO-designate Ashiss Kumar Dash's first results commentary as a new variable
rejected_candidates.detail: No directional content. Any tone from him lands on the guide and is covered by finding 1.

rejected_candidates.candidate: Large-deal TCV expected at $2-3bn, against $3.6bn in Q1 and $14.9bn in Q4 FY26
rejected_candidates.detail: This is the consensus bar, not a fact about the print. It is carried in 'bar'.

baseline_tension: The negative lean on the guide agrees with the +5 put skew, so it is partly priced. The +24% 20-day run-up cuts both ways: it makes a trim more costly but was built alongside a 109M-ADR short that is still covering. Net, the evidence does not beat the skew, and p_up sits only slightly below 50.
lessons_applied: Rule 6 (bar disputed): the guide bar has two broker expectations that disagree (1.5-2.5% against 2-3%), so finding 1 was capped from -1.5 to -1.0

Rule 7 (crowded short, sign agreeing with skew): finding 2 went from -0.5 to -0.3 because it restates the baseline run-up into a short of 109M ADRs; p_up moved from 45 to 47, so expected_move_pct went from -0.70 to -0.42
'A reaction history built from the wrong events': already handled before reading. The base rate was rebuilt from the four confirmed releases and the baseline history moved to rejected_candidates
Rules 1 and 5 left the reported-quarter (+0.3), peer (+0.5), short-interest (+0.8) and wage-hike (-0.3) findings unchanged
